ctx.intro: The `ctx` argument handed to the script's `func run(ctx):`. Registered in register_types.cpp (SCENE level, TOOLS_ENABLED block). v2 carries the full frozen ctx stdlib from doc/SUMMER/SCENE_SCRIPTING_CONTRACTS.md: every creation helper adds to the edited scene root when no parent is given, sets owner to the edited scene root by default (the #1 silent persistence gotcha, made structurally impossible), and returns the created node. `props` dictionaries apply via set() per key; keys that match no property are collected into the `prop_warnings` report entry, never silently dropped.

Same conventions (owner-by-default, return the node, prop_warnings, structured report entries on failure — never silent). 2D helpers work in any edited scene (root may be Node2D or Node); Control helpers parent under the edited root unless a parent is given.

Gameplay-code lane. All three write OUTSIDE the scene (files, project settings): covered by the pre-run checkpoint only, never by the packed-scene undo step — surfaced through the result's files_written / project_settings_changed + undo_action_note.

methods.section: Wave H game completeness ctx v4 (frozen API, SCENE_SCRIPTING_CONTRACTS.md)
methods.signature: make_prefab(node: Node, path: String, replace_with_instance: bool = true) -> Node
methods.description: Packs the node's subtree to a PackedScene at path (owner fix-up first: descendants owned by the edited root are re-owned to the node for the pack and ALWAYS put back; the node's own position is zeroed for the pack and restored, like the editor's Save Branch), saves, registers the file.

op.name: RunSceneScript
op.registry_description: Compile and run one AI-authored GDScript in-process on the editor main thread against the live edited scene.
op.header_intro: RunSceneScript — compile and run one AI-authored GDScript in-process against the live edited scene.

params.name: checkpoint
params.description: request a SummerGit checkpoint before execution. Honored only with checkpointCapabilityEnabled:true, and a missing checkpoint NEVER blocks the run (no_rewind_point pattern).

params.name: checkpointCapabilityEnabled
params.description: the capability gate read alongside checkpoint (op.get("checkpointCapabilityEnabled", false)): a checkpoint is attempted only when BOTH are true; false -> checkpoint:{ok:false, reason:"checkpoint_capability_disabled"} and the run proceeds un-rewindable. Same gate as RunEditorScript's pre-run checkpoint (editor_script_ops.h).

params.name: max_seconds
params.description: HARD wall-clock budget: the GDScript VM deadline guard raises "Summer script budget exceeded (Ns)." at the first loop edge past the deadline (also still surfaced cooperatively via ctx.frames_budget_exceeded()). Blocking single calls (delays, awaits, native code) are outside the guard's reach.

params.name: script_source
params.description: GDScript defining `func run(ctx):`. If it has no `extends` line we prepend `extends RefCounted`, and if it has no `@tool` we prepend `@tool` (a non-tool script only gets a placeholder instance in the editor and never runs); both are REPORTED back in `normalizations`, never silent.

params.name: undo
params.description: "action" snapshots the edited scene around the run: a GDScript runtime error restores the pre-run state (rolled_back:true) and a successful run registers ONE editor undo step covering the whole script (see the design block at the top of this header for exact coverage). "none" keeps v1 behavior (checkpoint only).

op.ctx_listing_text: The ctx handed to run() carries the frozen stdlib (SCENE_SCRIPTING_CONTRACTS Waves C + F): get_scene_root, report, set_owner_recursive, frames_budget_exceeded, add_node, find, get_or_create, instance_scene, add_mesh (box|sphere|capsule|cylinder|plane|torus|text), add_mesh_with_collision, mesh_from_arrays, make_material, apply_material, grid, scatter, add_light_rig, ensure_environment, add_camera, summary, save_scene, plus the geometry stdlib v2: boolean, extrude_polygon, lathe, sweep, set_smooth, terrain, decimate, convex_collision, uv_planar, uv_box, mirror, animate, make_shader, plus the Wave G animation stdlib (ctx v3): animate v2 (per-key {interpolation: "nearest"|"linear"|"cubic"} — per-track in Animation, first keyed mode wins; bone targets "<skeleton>:<bone>/position|rotation|scale"; blend shapes via value tracks on "blend_shapes/<name>"), animate_method (method-call tracks), anim_state_machine (AnimationTree + AnimationNodeStateMachine over the player's clips), bone_pose, look_at_modifier, plus the Wave H game completeness stdlib (ctx v4): 2D — add_sprite, add_animated_sprite, add_tilemap, paint_tiles, paint_rect, add_body_2d, add_camera_2d, add_parallax; UI — add_ui, add_canvas_layer, set_theme_overrides, connect_signal (CONNECT_PERSIST, saved into the .tscn); gameplay-code lane — attach_script (validate -> write -> load -> set_script), make_prefab (pack a subtree to its own .tscn, optionally swap for an instance), add_autoload, add_input_action, set_main_scene. Creation helpers own-by-default and return the node; unknown props keys land in the `prop_warnings` report entry.
op.returns_text:
{ ok, op:"RunSceneScript", ran, result:<script return value>,
     reports:<ctx dict>, output:[String], stderr:[String], errors:[String],
     lines_truncated:int (count of output/stderr/errors lines dropped past the
     capture caps; 0 when nothing was dropped),
     duration_ms, checkpoint:{...}, normalizations:[String], line_offset,
     had_edited_scene, budget_exceeded, budget_enforced,
     rolled_back (undo:"action" only), undo_action:"registered"|"unavailable"
     (+ undo_unavailable_reason), rollback_error (only when a rollback was
     attempted and failed) }
   plus no_rewind_point:true + no_rewind_reason:String when no checkpoint
   exists, plus — only when a Wave H helper wrote outside the scene —
   files_written:[res:// paths], project_settings_changed:[keys] and
   undo_action_note:String stating that those are covered by the pre-run
   checkpoint ONLY (neither the undo step nor an error rollback touches
   files on disk or project.godot). The parse_error failure additionally
   carries parse_errors:[{line, column, message}] from the compile-first
   validation, line numbers relative to the normalized source (see
   line_offset).

result_fields.name: budget_enforced
result_fields.note: Whether the hard VM deadline guard was armed for this run.

result_fields.name: budget_exceeded
result_fields.note: true when the run passed `max_seconds` (soft check, VM guard or measured duration).

result_fields.name: checkpoint
result_fields.note: The SummerGit checkpoint result when one was requested and taken.

result_fields.name: duration_ms
result_fields.note: Wall-clock time of the run in milliseconds.

result_fields.name: error
result_fields.note: Human-readable failure text (failures and runtime errors only).

result_fields.name: errors
result_fields.note: Script error messages raised during the run (capped, see limits).

result_fields.name: failure_reason
result_fields.note: Machine-readable failure class (see below).

result_fields.name: files_written
result_fields.note: res:// paths a helper wrote outside the scene (only when it happened).

result_fields.name: had_edited_scene
result_fields.note: Whether a scene was open when the script ran.

result_fields.name: line_offset
result_fields.note: How many lines the normalizations shifted the script's line numbers by.

result_fields.name: lines_truncated
result_fields.note: true when `output` or `errors` hit their line caps and later lines were dropped.

result_fields.name: no_rewind_point
result_fields.note: true when no checkpoint exists for this run.

result_fields.name: no_rewind_reason
result_fields.note: Why no checkpoint exists (only with `no_rewind_point`).

result_fields.name: normalizations
result_fields.note: What was prepended to the source (`@tool`, `extends RefCounted`) — never silent.

result_fields.name: ok
result_fields.note: true when the script compiled, ran and raised no script error.

result_fields.name: op
result_fields.note: Always "RunSceneScript".

result_fields.name: output
result_fields.note: Captured `print()` lines (capped, see limits).

result_fields.name: parse_errors
result_fields.note: parse_error only — the compile-first validation's `[{line, column, message}]`, relative to the normalized source.

result_fields.name: project_settings_changed
result_fields.note: project.godot keys a helper changed (only when it happened).

result_fields.name: ran
result_fields.note: true when `run(ctx)` was actually entered (false on compile/instantiate failures).

result_fields.name: reports
result_fields.note: The `ctx.report()` dictionary plus helper-written entries such as `prop_warnings`.

result_fields.name: result
result_fields.note: The script's return value, sanitized for JSON.

result_fields.name: rollback_error
result_fields.note: Only when a rollback was attempted and failed; the scene may hold half-applied changes.

result_fields.name: rolled_back
result_fields.note: undo:"action" only — true when a runtime error restored the pre-run scene.

result_fields.name: stderr
result_fields.note: Captured error-stream lines.

result_fields.name: undo_action
result_fields.note: "registered" when one editor undo step covers the run, else "unavailable".

result_fields.name: undo_action_note
result_fields.note: States that files/settings are covered by the checkpoint only (only when they were written).

result_fields.name: undo_unavailable_reason
result_fields.note: Why no undo step could be registered (only with undo_action:"unavailable").

design_block: [SUMMER] RunSceneScript op — in-process scene scripting, the
execute_blender_code equivalent.
Runs one AI-authored GDScript IN THIS EDITOR PROCESS, on the editor main
thread, against the LIVE edited scene. This is deliberately the opposite
trade to RunEditorScript (editor/ops/editor_script_ops.h), which spawns a
short-lived headless CHILD editor: the child is killable but blind to the
live scene tree; this op sees and mutates the open scene directly, exactly
like typing into a bpy console, at the cost of sharing our main thread.
THE ACCEPTED RISK, RESTATED FOR v2
v1 accepted that a `while true:` in the supplied script wedges the editor
main thread. v2 mitigates the wedge with a fork-only HARD budget: the
GDScript VM's backward-jump path checks an armed wall-clock deadline
(GDScriptLanguage::summer_arm_exec_deadline, modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp)
and raises the script error "Summer script budget exceeded (Ns)." at the
first loop edge past the deadline. Every GDScript loop construct passes a
backward OPCODE_JUMP once per iteration, so any loop-shaped wedge is caught;
what the guard canNOT catch is a single opcode that blocks by itself
(OS.delay_msec(1e9), a blocking await on a signal that never fires, or a
wedge inside a native call). Those remain accepted: there is still no safe
way to preempt a synchronous native call on the LIVE editor's main thread.
Result field `budget_enforced` reports honestly whether the guard was armed.
UNDO / ROLLBACK (v2), THE DESIGN ACTUALLY SHIPPED
Recording true do/undo pairs for arbitrary script effects is impractical —
the script mutates the scene directly, not through an API we can intercept.
Instead, with undo:"action" (the default) the op snapshots the SAVABLE state
of the edited scene (PackedScene::pack of the edited root) before and after
the run:
* on a GDScript runtime error the BEFORE state is restored immediately and
the result carries rolled_back:true (rolled_back:false + rollback_error
if the restore itself failed — the result never claims a rollback it did
not perform);
* on success ONE undo step is registered on the edited scene's
EditorUndoRedoManager history whose undo/redo closures re-instantiate
the before/after snapshots, so human Ctrl+Z reverts the whole run. When
the op executor already holds an open action for this op, the step is
folded into it (it surfaces under the op's action name); a direct caller
outside an executor action gets a step named "AI: Scene Script".
EXACT COVERAGE, honestly stated: the snapshot round-trips exactly what
SaveScene would persist — nodes owned by the edited root (instanced child
scenes collapse to their instance reference, as in a .tscn). NOT covered:
nodes the script left unowned (invisible to pack(), exactly as they are
invisible to save), edits to EXTERNAL resources or files on disk (undo
covers the scene, not the filesystem — that is what the SummerGit checkpoint
is for), and editor-only state (selection, folding). Undo/redo/rollback
replace the scene root with a fresh instantiation, so node references from
before the restore go stale. If a snapshot cannot be taken (pack error, no
scene history), the result says so via undo_action:"unavailable" — the run
still executes. undo:"none" skips all snapshots (checkpoint-only, v1
behavior).
